This is one reading turn of an openness review of the exact statement in reading_turn.statement. Each turn is a fresh input without earlier conversation. Read everything delivered now completely; do not judge openness until the final turn.

reading_turn.reading_plan lists delivered_before, delivered_now and remaining. The bodies of delivered_now are in evidence. A unit has a kind and identity: fulltext uses version_id; search_response uses source_id; record uses record_kind and record_id. record_kind is literature_search, reading or problem_statement. Full texts and captured responses may also specify text_sha256, identifying the whole stored body. Use that hash when supplied. A historical plan entry without kind is a full text. Store records arrive as their exact JSON text. In this problem review, full texts arrive before the packet's records.

One reading turn delivers at most 120,000 characters of new unit text. A larger body arrives in consecutive parts. Each plan entry gives part, parts, start, end and characters; start and end are character offsets in the whole body, and its artifact identifies the delivered whole body or slice. A delivered unit or part need not appear again.

reading_turn.reading_record carries earlier notes, checked excerpts, passage answers and allowances. Its sources list gives one whole-source descriptor per cited artifact, with the identities that name it. A verified excerpt or delivered passage gives its exact source text, character offsets start and end, and the SHA-256 of that span's UTF-8 bytes. Unmatched excerpts are your own unchecked copies. Passage answers identify their requesting assignment and request ID.

To fit the route input limit, later turns may withhold the notes of the earliest turns, replacing notes with notes_withheld. The final turn may first withhold bodies delivered complete in earlier reading turns, with a note naming those turns. The harness never withholds an excerpt or a passage. The statement, formulations and allowances remain. Keep what the judgment needs as excerpts, and carry essential conclusions and unresolved issues from earlier notes into your latest notes.

Return exactly {schema_version:1,stage:"reading",subject_digest,claim_digest,reviewer,excerpts,notes,passage_requests}. Copy subject_digest, claim_digest and reviewer exactly from reading_turn. notes is a nonempty string of at most 20,000 characters explaining what the delivered material establishes, what remains open, and its bearing on the statement and every formulation in reading_turn.formulations.

excerpts is a list of {version_id,text,purpose}, {source_id,text,purpose}, or {record_kind,record_id,text,purpose}. The first two forms may include text_sha256. Do not mix identity forms. Copy definitions, normalizations, relevant results with every hypothesis, open or solved statements, and material record details such as queries, coverage, dispositions and reading notes. purpose briefly explains why the quotation matters. Copy record text from the JSON body, including escapes inside its strings, rather than from a reconstructed field value.

The harness matches against the whole stored body after changing each character to its NFKC form, collapsing whitespace runs and trimming outer whitespace. It uses the first match and returns the original source characters. An excerpt needs at least 20 normalized characters and its matched original span must be at most 6,000 characters. A missing source, absent match or invalid length produces status "unmatched" with a reason. Verified excerpts consume at most 200,000 original characters over the chain; an otherwise matching excerpt beyond that allowance has status "over_allowance" and no delivered text.

passage_requests is a possibly empty list of {id,<the same identity fields>,anchor,characters}. IDs are unique within this response. anchor is a verbatim phrase of at least 20 normalized characters. characters is an integer from 1 to 20,000. The next turn returns original text starting at the first matching anchor, up to that length and the end of the body, or status "not_found". Delivered passages consume at most 100,000 characters over the chain; a passage exceeding the remaining allowance has status "over_allowance" and no delivered text. reading_turn.reading_record.allowances shows both totals and their usage. Excerpts and passages do not establish complete reading of a unit.
